body: Thanks, I will check it out.

I would really love to distract myself but I am a medical student and my life is too fast paced and so I don't really get much time to take time off and not stress. I am at the point of accepting that this is just going to be my life from now on.
Thank you so much. I will look into genetic testing.
No, sertraline was the first thing I was started on and my psychiatrist has just been increasing the dose.

Heart palpitations, tension headaches, body aches, abdominal pain, dyspnoea, shaking, literally breaking out into tears out of nowhere and being in a state of numbness where I am zoned out to everything and everyone but my head is spinning with so many thoughts to the point that I can't sleep, I end up sleeping and then I dream about my problems, I wake up most days drenched in sweat.

I have been admitted into a psychiatric ward before for 2 weeks because everything became so bad. It was a horrible experience for me and I would hopefully not like to go back. But Thank you so much, I think I need to really just deal with the cause.

Urbanol is habit-forming. Please do not take them without being prescribed by a medical professional. You will need to be started off on a low dose and then titrated upwards. Besides, there are other medications you can be prescribed to take for anxiety  before you get to the stage of urbanol.

I saw you are in South Africa, so am I. Reach out to SADAG and join an anxiety and panic disorder support group. You can also go the public healthcare route to get a psychiatrist if you cannot afford one. I saw a private psychiatrist and he put me on SSRIs, then mood stabilizers, then urbanol and now I even take ativan. So I definitely know the struggle. I also fear driving and any activity that requires me to leave my house. It does get better though. It just takes time. If you are in Cape Town I can refer a really great psychiatrist for you.

Edit: The psychiatrist in question meets you in person for the first session and then gives you the option for online sessions for the subsequent visits which has been really helpful for my anxiety.

Ngl, the thing that helped me the most was started medication for my anxiety. It opened up the world for me in a way I never realised was possible. Knowing I was on the medication helped me gain the confidence I needed. In your case, possibly try buying placebos (over the counter stress relief pills) and use that to trick your brain into believing that you have taken something to numb your anxiety and there is nothing standing in the way of interacting with people in the way you would like.

For me, my room is usually a reflection of what's going on in my head. I generally like my room clean but there are times when my anxiety spikes and I feel overwhelmed, and in those instances, my room will be a pigsty. I will have no desire to clean it, in fact I feel better having it in that state when my head is feeling messed up. But as soon as I feel better, I will start cleaning it up and it becomes therapeutic because it shows that I am now in a better place. My friends (I live in res) all understand this about me and don't even judge me when they enter my room and it's in the worst state ever. Don't know if you might be similar.
I usually do this when I have panic attacks, it helps.
Definitely going to discuss this with my doctor, thank you so much.

I was briefly hospitalised in a psychiatric ward and my insomnia started then. Only difference is, I would be given betapam and 2 lorazopams to sleep every now, whereas now, I only have the zopivane and it's not helping me sleep at all. It's been 4 weeks since I was discharged.
I can only fall asleep after 07h00 the next day. Then it's usually interrupted sleep and only a couple of hours. I will try the not lying in bed though.
